clue.text: A bit of fatty food, say, in B&B, given to everyone

indicators.note: the word for 'say' sits inside the two Bs of B&B

parts.note: B&B, bed and breakfast, supplies its two Bs
to say something is to utter it
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A greasy treat served up to every guest at a bed and breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: B&B is a British bed-and-breakfast guesthouse; here it just gives two Bs. 'given to' joins the last piece on.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a small pat or ball of butter, which is a fatty food, so it is a bit of one.

clue.text: Hairstyle that is a hit

definitions.meaning: a fringe, in American usage, cut straight across the forehead
a blow or thump, also a loud noise

explanation.surface: A haircut that proves a great success.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a fringe of hair this, and a blow or knock is also this.

clue.text: Portray me being silly — here today, gone tomorrow

indicators.note: silly behaviour scrambles things, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be painted in a daft way, knowing fame is fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something transient, lasting only a short while, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: German city being without Anglican church

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the church letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: essence is one's being, one's fundamental nature
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A city in Germany that has no Church of England congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: Hard cheese naughty lad fed to male rabbit?

indicators.note: food fed to the animal goes inside it, so these letters go into the rabbit word

parts.note: a male rabbit is a buck

indicators.note: a naughty child misbehaves, so the letters of lad are put out of order

explanation.surface: A mischievous boy gives cheese to a buck rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese' is British slang for bad luck, a phrase of mock sympathy; 'naughty' makes ADL from lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard cheese is a British idiom used to commiserate with someone over misfortune.

clue.text: Blow with awful rain as sheet upon sheet

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard, and a lam is a blow

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly done, so the letters of rain are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gale with dreadful rain comes down in sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' makes INAR from rain; 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminar means arranged in thin layers or plates, one sheet lying on another.

clue.text: This person backed Irish ruler

indicators.note: backed means going in reverse, so the self-reference is read backwards

parts.note: this person is the setter, me

explanation.surface: The speaker supported an Irish leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or commander, a ruler in parts of the Middle East.

clue.text: Three leading characters from Cambridge set up a university somewhere in China

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read upwards, so those letters run backwards
the leading characters are the first three letters of the city

explanation.surface: Three Cambridge figures found a university in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three leading characters from' Cambridge are CAM, and 'set up' turns them to MAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Macau is a special administrative region on the south coast of China, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Puddings making one poorly somehow? Stories!

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of poorly are put together in some other way

parts.note: stories are lies, untruths

explanation.surface: Someone claims puddings made them ill, but it is all tall tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' makes ROLYPO from poorly; 'making one' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Roly-poly is a traditional British suet pudding rolled up with jam, so several are puddings.

clue.text: In school period it amounts to pause

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year

explanation.surface: Over a school term, a break adds up to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to stop for a while, to suspend or interrupt, which is pausing.

clue.text: Revolutionary house name in French city

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the house word is turned back to front

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: A house in a French city bears a radical name.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house; 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimes is a city in southern France known for its Roman arena.

clue.text: Sunday's social event — small, with calories cut down

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
mini means small

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so the word calories loses its tail

explanation.surface: A Sunday party, kept modest and with a low-calorie menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominical means relating to the Lord's day, as in a dominical letter in church calendars.

clue.text: Maybe Bangor's act is in decline

parts.note: Bangor is a town in County Down, so its county is Down
a turn is a performer's act

explanation.surface: A performance in the Welsh or Ulster town is going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangor in Northern Ireland lies in County Down; 'Maybe' flags the town as one example. The obvious Bangor is the Welsh one.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturn is a fall in activity or fortunes, especially economic, which is a decline.

clue.text: Give everything needed to English queen, one with limited power

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: limited means cut back, so power keeps only its first letter

explanation.surface: Supplying an English queen whose authority is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish them with whatever they require.

clue.text: Tool said to have succeeded getting in

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the S slips in between the other pieces

parts.note: spoke is said, the past of speak
to have gives the verb have
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A tool reportedly managed to get inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokeshave is a woodworker's small two-handled plane for shaping curved pieces such as wheel spokes.

clue.text: Bird seed by pile of hay

indicators.note: by means next to, so the hay word sits beside the seed

parts.note: a pea is a seed of the pea plant
a cock is a small conical heap of hay, a haycock

explanation.surface: A bird pecking at seed beside a haystack.
explanation.definitionFit: The peacock is the male peafowl, a showy bird famous for its fanned tail.

clue.text: Experienced folk — arthritic strugglers when pen has to be put to paper?

definitions.meaning: veterans, people long practised at something

definitions.text: arthritic strugglers when pen has to be put to paper?
definitions.meaning: the aged fingers that find writing difficult

explanation.surface: Veterans whose stiff fingers struggle to write.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans are called this idiomatically, and literally aged fingers struggle with a pen.

clue.text: Sixties teenager in dance showing style again

indicators.note: in places the teenager inside the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
a mod was a stylish 1960s British youth

explanation.surface: A Sixties youth at a dance shows off a new look.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a 1960s British youth subculture of sharp suits and scooters; 'showing' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To remodel is to reshape or restyle something, giving it a fresh form.

clue.text: Hat priced ridiculously, attractive to potential buyer?

indicators.note: ridiculously means absurdly, so the letters of the two words are put in a crazy order

explanation.surface: A hat at an absurd price, tempting a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very cheap appeals to bargain hunters, which is why the question mark hedges the definition.

clue.text: Tense, with higher notes having to be sung?

definitions.text: with higher notes having to be sung?
definitions.meaning: music shifted into a higher key, made literal

explanation.surface: A nervous singer facing a score set high.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anxious and excited is described this way, and a song transposed upward is literally this.

clue.text: Like many an egg taken illegally

definitions.meaning: cooked by simmering out of the shell in water
hunted game or fish illegally, or stolen

explanation.surface: An egg obtained by theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are often cooked this gentle way, and game taken without a right is also this.

clue.text: Spooner's worry, notice, is no longer confined

indicators.note: Spooner swapped initial sounds of words, so the opening letters of the two words trade places

parts.note: to fret is to worry
to see is to notice

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner frets, then notices he has been released.
explanation.definitionFit: Released or liberated, the phrase describes a captive who is now unconfined.

clue.text: Tot crossing river in a South American country

indicators.note: crossing means going across, so the sum word stretches over the other pieces

parts.note: to tot up is to sum, and a tot is a sum

explanation.surface: A small child wading over a river somewhere in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Surinam, now usually Suriname, is a country on the north-east coast of South America.

clue.text: In the morning soldiers knocked over character in Athens

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: AM means in the morning
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops in the morning flattened something in Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a letter used in Athens.

clue.text: Good alternative to roads is what some look for

parts.note: rail transport is an alternative to roads

explanation.surface: Commuters weighing up trains against roads and seeking something.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail is a sought object of legend, and figuratively any longed-for goal.

clue.text: Care is arranged, old boy being kept inside for exercises

indicators.note: being kept inside places the old boy within the reordered letters
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of care and is are reordered

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A carer arranges a workout with a former pupil kept indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes AERICS from care and is; 'being kept inside' puts OB within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobics are vigorous rhythmic exercises meant to build cardiovascular fitness.

clue.text: A thin flat piece turned over in wood

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: a slab is a flat piece of stone or wood

explanation.surface: A flat piece of timber flipped over in a woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light tropical wood, popular for model-making.

clue.text: Fair one is in shipping bulletin I will broadcast

definitions.text: Fair one is in shipping bulletin

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out on air, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: I will contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: A radio announcer promises to read the shipping forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is a sea area in the BBC Shipping Forecast, the British radio bulletin of sea weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair Isle is a Scottish island named in the shipping forecast, so the fair one is an island.

clue.text: At some stage a yellowish-brown bird will nibble worm's head

parts.note: sand is a pale yellowish-brown colour

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: Sooner or later a sandy-coloured bird will peck at a worm.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at some unspecified future time, if and when it happens.

clue.text: City weeps when leader is lost

indicators.note: losing the leader means the first letter goes

parts.note: something that bleeds oozes or weeps

explanation.surface: A city in tears after its leader dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Lengths of cloth to dispose of, first to last

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter is shifted to the end

parts.note: to sell something is to dispose of it

explanation.surface: Bolts of fabric to be got rid of in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure of cloth length, about 45 inches in England.

clue.text: Fruit from old garden creating lump in the throat

definitions.meaning: the forbidden fruit Adam took in Eden
the visible bulge of the larynx at the front of the neck

explanation.surface: Eating fruit from an old orchard brings on a choking emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the throat bulge is a piece of the forbidden fruit stuck in Adam's throat.
